title: Durable infrastructure and agent access
summary: Shared Rust request/receipt verification, browser-local acceptance and a bounded image requester are implemented. Proposed goals cover durable operations, authenticated transport, cancellation and recovery, full MCP access and separately scoped workflow validation.

goals.title: Requester protocol and local outcomes
goals.description: Implemented signed evidence sessions and browser-local retention, inspection and acceptance. These foundations do not establish hosted durability, cross-device synchronization or global replay exclusion.

milestones.title: Implement the shared requester protocol and browser adapter
milestones.description: The Rust evidence-session API supports image, location, camera/location composition and audio. Signed requests freeze operator pins, policy and delivery limits; receipts bind original authority, exact artifacts, transcript, context and requester-observed arrival. AgentRequester supplies start, receive, verify, inspect, accept and cancel through the shared Rust/WASM worker. Its identity and ledgers remain local to the browser origin/profile. Active sessions close on page suspension rather than resuming elapsed timing; completed records can be inspected without new collection. Caller adapters still own transport, consent and collector cleanup. This is an implemented local foundation, not a hosted recovery or authorization service.
acceptance: The shared Rust protocol authenticates the retained original request and requester pin, reruns actual artifact appraisal and separates signature validity, policy satisfaction, freshness and acceptance.
The browser adapter reserves session and sensor nonce before dispatch, retains exact completed evidence and context, and reverifies stored originals for inspection and explicit acceptance.

Local acceptance checks unchanged stored bytes, lifecycle authority, expiry and the current verification second before atomically adding unique session and challenge records; Rust verification itself records no acceptance or replay protection.
Retained inspection preserves historical evidence and matching local acceptance without renewing freshness or restarting an interrupted session.

evidence.label: Implemented session API and local acceptance boundary
Local reservation, retention and atomic acceptance implementation

milestones.title: Validate synthetic audio retention and concurrent local acceptance
milestones.description: The 8 October software checkpoint passed six Chromium checks using signed synthetic PCM, actual Rust/WASM verification and two tabs sharing one same-origin IndexedDB ledger. Both tabs verified before either committed; exactly one first acceptance won. Guard cancellation after verification and inside the transaction left both acceptance keys absent, and reload/replay preserved exact originals and the winning rows. No WebRTC, AudioWorklet, physical microphone or speaker ran in this concurrency check. The separate 7 October integration covered synthetic WebRTC/AudioWorklet and reload, without restoring the audio page's final export controls. Physical requester/operator acceptance is deferred until a second device is available; cleared storage, other profiles/devices and hidden histories remain outside local replay protection.
acceptance: Independent re-verification uses retained authority, original policy and exact completed bytes in the covered local workflow.
Concurrent first acceptance in two same-origin tabs commits exactly once in the identified local ledger.

Lifecycle-guard cancellation after verification and inside the transaction leaves acceptance keys absent; reload/replay checks reverify unchanged retained bytes and preserve winning rows without a new request, round, probe or signing.

7 October synthetic integration, reload and retained failed assertion

goals.title: Bounded separate-process image requester
goals.description: A Debian CLI adapter and a recorded computer/phone USB receipt demonstration. Neither supplies a resumable service, authenticated device workflow transport or acceptance ledger.

milestones.title: Implement the image requester CLI prototype
milestones.description: One uninterrupted Debian process uses the shipped Rust/WASM protocol, creates its requester identity before dispatch and retains exact policy, context, request, returned JPEG, arrival observations and signed receipt. Dispatch witnesses stdout handoff to the caller; arrival is witnessed only after the process reads the complete file. The private requester key is memory-only. Existing output directories cannot resume or be overwritten. The adapter has no phone control, transport service, restart recovery or acceptance store; synthetic software-fixture checks do not establish physical capture.
acceptance: Explicit dispatch, receive and cancel commands use shared Rust verification and bounded original timing rather than caller-provided arrival timestamps.
Original policy/context and exact returned evidence are retained; successful completion requires receipt reverification and fresh eligibility without recording local or global acceptance.
The process rejects changed authority, duplicate delivery, missed deadlines and existing output directories, retaining failure records when writable.

evidence.label: CLI behavior, timing and recovery limits
Synthetic real-WASM and actual CLI-process test definitions

milestones.title: Record one computer-requester phone-image receipt over USB
milestones.description: The authored USB history records six incomplete attempts separately and a successful seventh run: the separate computer requester received the complete 2,677,097-byte phone JPEG in 120,785 ms within the original 180,000 ms limit, verified it and signed/reverified its receipt. The approved USB helper delivered the bare camera challenge; the handset UI did not authenticate the CLI's signed requester wrapper. This demonstrates that bounded image path, not live UI pairing, deployed agent transport, replay acceptance, raw GNSS, remote attestation, trusted clocks or physical scene authenticity. Detailed operational evidence remains private.
acceptance: The recorded seventh run completed exact challenge insertion, native shutter, signed JPEG saving/export and complete-file reception before the unchanged response deadline.
C2PA integrity, original request/operator binding, GPS and native camera metadata, correlated camera clock, requester receipt authentication and timing checks passed in that run.

evidence.label: Authored USB attempt history and scoped physical result
Workflow architecture distinguishes USB result from failed live-channel preflight

goals.title: Full authorized workflow access through MCP
goals.description: Proposed future work, following the owner's 30 September direction: expose the complete authorized evidence lifecycle, from capability discovery and preparation through dispatch, status, cancellation, exact originals, verification, explicit evidence acceptance and retained inspection, without screen automation. Reuse the shared Rust verifier through MCP, CLI and UI adapters. Define operation/error/grant/result schemas, supported SDK/protocol revision, MCP transport/authentication and long-operation status behavior. Distinguish file delivery, verification/freshness and evidence-ledger acceptance from Assignment formation, exact proposal/Contract signatures, completion acknowledgment, ballot authorization/admission, collective policy approval, settlement effects, payment and case closure. Assignments, Dispute procedure and the Operators union define their respective action meanings and permissions; storing or delivering a record, account login and delegated device access establish none of those effects. Whether consequential actions enter MCP requires explicit domain scope and authority decisions with Identity and Governance. No expanded signing authority, deployment or sensor use is authorized here.

milestones.title: Define owner-requested MCP workflow access
milestones.description: The recorded operation groups cover discovery, enrollment/policy, preparation, dispatch, status/cancellation, evidence verification, separate acceptance and recovery/retention. They are requirements, not implemented MCP tools. Final operation/error/grant/result schemas, supported SDK/protocol revision and transport/authentication choices still need definition. Browser pin/signature checks do not implement principal-scoped service grants or revocation. No MCP endpoint, durable hosted requester/acceptance ledger, cross-device recovery or global replay exclusion is established. Existing same-origin races are synthetic local checks, not two remote agents racing a hosted ledger. No owner, dependencies or implementation start date are confirmed.

evidence.label: Recorded owner direction and implementation limits

goals.title: Durable operations and acceptance across devices
goals.description: Proposed future work: define the shared workflow state, operation identity, synchronization, exact-input idempotency, conflict, lost-response lookup and uncertain-effect contract for durable requests, original policy/context, evidence and acceptance. Decide ledger authority/replay scope, concurrent acceptance and inspection after restart without renewing challenges or recreating elapsed timing. Server side services implements the authoritative hosted records, atomic transactions, exchange endpoints, access enforcement and operating recovery against that contract; Identity defines account/key authority. Domain uniqueness, including the first-version one-Assignment-per-Request rule, needs Assignments' formation semantics and a selected authoritative service registry; operation keys alone establish no global uniqueness. Lookup/retry must preserve original action, authority and policy versions without another signature, renewed ballot consent, withdrawal of an earlier signature, reversal of an irrevocable release or invented case closure. Dispute procedure and the Operators union supply their respective effect, correction and finality rules. Represent delivery, reading, acknowledgment and consent separately; Dispute procedure and Material incidents define sufficient domain notice, Identity supplies silent clock-out/sign-out policy, Assignments supplies participant presentation and Server side services implements selected delivery. Their reconciliation must not resume sensing. Storage, retention and recovery designs remain unresolved, and a local exactly-once commit promises no exactly-once network delivery.

goals.title: Authenticated device transport and delegated access
goals.description: Proposed future work: connect authorized requester agents and operator devices independently of a visible webpage or a particular peer transport, preserving exact bytes, dispatch/complete-arrival observations, original deadlines and cancellation. MCP client/server authentication and requester/operator transport are separate choices. Identity owns principal/device/key authority, delegation and hold/clock-out/sign-out policy; this Hero defines grant representation, validity/revocation propagation, operation scoping and observed shutdown semantics. A grant or pending resume decision must bind the authoritative account work-state revision to principal, device, operation, purpose, sensors, recipients, explicit consent and validity bounds. The deliberate authentication-camera exception remains scoped to its initiating device, operation and current revision, granting no work resumption. Server side services implements hosted authority/enforcement where selected; APK buildout implements the reviewed narrow Android connection and native enforcement. Scope status, artifact, cancel and accept lookups to the caller's grant. Reconnect, cached authentication or stale grants must not undo work privacy or restart sensing; unreachable devices remain unconfirmed. Authority provenance, offline bounds, conflicts and sign-out invalidation remain Identity decisions. Any maintained navigation/attestation-input distribution requires separately chosen independent sources/trust policy and cannot silently replace original verifier context. No transport, grant schema or provider is selected.

goals.title: Cancellation, cleanup and inspectable failed attempts
goals.description: Proposed future work: define per-operation resource ownership, cancellation acknowledgement versus confirmed shutdown, conflicting device operations and preservation of partial or completed evidence. Consume Sensor hardening's actual per-component phase/outcome, exact request/profile association, report availability/signature state, observed terminal timing and cleanup state; expose retained ownership or unknown release honestly. Unavailable/unassessable quality, partial/failed collection and a complete artifact are different results, and a signed failure proves no fault or payment consequence. APK buildout maps permission, foreground/unlock waits and native resource outcomes to the shared contract; Server side services supplies hosted retention. Preserve original deadlines and policy, distinguish preparation from qualifying observations, and keep read-only status from renewing warm-up or activating sensors. Active interrupted sessions close; inspection, lost-response lookup or reconnect must not restart collection. Resume alternatives, terminal cleanup guarantees and export/deletion authority remain unresolved. Broader sensor failure formats and physical cleanup evidence belong to Sensor hardening and APK, without a parallel trial plan here.

goals.title: Agent workflow conformance and domain validation handoffs
goals.description: Proposed future work: own software workflow/MCP conformance for wrong-principal access, grant revocation, duplicate/conflicting calls, lost responses, stale evidence, declared-ledger concurrency, cancellation and disconnect/crash outcomes. Define a bounded agent demonstration of request, exact-file receipt, reverification, explicit acceptance and retained inspection after reconnect without UI automation. Artifact/status views must identify the supplied-history frontier and missing/redacted material without implying complete global history. Use shared evidence/case interfaces with dispute and incident views: Dispute procedure and Material incidents define their respective scrutiny, preservation, classification, referral and disclosure meanings, Identity defines general access/custody policy and Server side services implements selected records/exchange. Preservation and urgent-assistance handoffs must not await final incident classification; transport status establishes no fault, liability or coverage. Sensor hardening owns physical evidence acceptance, APK buildout owns Android lifecycle/update acceptance, Server side services owns hosted transaction/operational validation, and domain Heroes validate their action/procedure meanings. Consume their scoped results without duplicating physical plans or completion claims. A proposed cross-Hero slice must name its primary Hero, contributors, supplied interfaces/dependencies and shared acceptance evidence; scenario, authority, service/device scope and acceptance criteria remain undecided. No new device operation, deployment or change to an existing sensor hold is authorized.
